text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are here because of a breast mass. Can you describe the mass in terms of its size, texture (hard or soft), and whether it is tender or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old woman. The patient noticed a mass in her left breast 4 weeks ago, which has rapidly increased in size. She denies any recent trauma or infections. No history of similar complaints in the past.

speaker: Doctor
text: A rapidly enlarging mass in a 48-year-old woman raises concern for malignancy or inflammatory conditions. Is the skin over the mass red, warm, or dimpled, and do you have any family history of breast cancer?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Presence of a left breast mass. I also have Rapid increase in size of the mass, No skin or nipple changes, No pain associated with the mass.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you. To help narrow down the differential, have you noticed any nipple discharge, and are you currently pregnant or breastfeeding? Additionally, does the mass feel fixed to the underlying tissue or is it mobile?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The ultrasound showing normal readings despite a rapidly enlarging mass is highly suspicious for a phyllodes tumor or other lesion not clearly visualized on initial imaging. I will proceed with a core needle biopsy to obtain a definitive tissue diagnosis.

REQUEST TEST: Core_Needle_Biopsy
